diagnosticOnly: This re-adjudication is DIAGNOSTIC and development-only. It is NOT used to make Stage-Q v2 pass and NOT used as a v3 qualification holdout.
rule: owner sufficiency definitions 2026-07-11; consistency SUPPORTED/PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED⇒SUFFICIENT, INCONCLUSIVE⇒INSUFFICIENT; assertion is not evidence for itself

changes.others: validity unchanged; RF7 sufficiency coordinate resolves the v2 ambiguity

exactEvidenceSpans: The section states its one job in the first line, gives a worked example, then a two-question check that maps to that job.
Evidence class: score-only. No chapter-level rationale supplied.
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: No change. The record is sufficient to assess the finding; the score-only complaint supplies no evidence and the passage is well aligned, so the finding is not established → UNSUPPORTED.

exactEvidenceSpans: Imagine, as a hypothetical, a manager who opens a review by asking what the team already knows is wrong.
The scene is explicitly invented to isolate the ordering.
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: No change. Sufficient to decide; the passage is explicitly hypothetical so the 'fabricated' allegation is not established → UNSUPPORTED.

exactEvidenceSpans: Q: Which step comes first? A) gather the facts  B) escalate  C) schedule a review. Answer key: B.
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: Validity unchanged (SUPPORTED). All quiz content is present (sufficient). The key marks B=escalate as the answer to 'which comes FIRST' while 'gather the facts' is the shown first option, and the explanation ('ensures visibility') justifies escalating but not escalating FIRST — a genuine quiz-key defect. AMBIGUITY: a strict reader (as one v2 judge did) can argue the materials do not FORMALLY prove the intended ordering, yielding UNSUPPORTED. Because reasonable adjudicators differ, this case is development-only and unfit as a qualification holdout.

exactEvidenceSpans: No such study is cited or supportable.
A 2016 Stanford study of 4,200 first-time managers found that those who ran weekly one-on-ones were 2.3 times more likely to retain their reports over two years.
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: CHANGED SUPPORTED→UNSUPPORTED (owner-directed). The record is sufficient to assess the FINDING. The finding merely ASSERTS invention ('No such study is cited or supportable') without supplying any evidence that establishes non-existence; an assertion is not evidence for itself, so the finding is not established → UNSUPPORTED. (This was my v2 gold-authoring error — the same assertion-vs-proof confusion that invalidated v1.)

exactEvidenceSpans: the demos alone turned the quarter around
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: No change. Sufficient to decide. Element (a) causal overreach is supported ('the demos alone turned the quarter around' = sole-causation); element (b) 'far too long' is refuted by the four-sentence passage. The finding materially overstates by bundling a false claim → PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.

exactEvidenceSpans: Consider a generic anonymous case: a team that ships on Fridays and spends Mondays on rollbacks.
The wording 'consider a generic case' frames it
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: CHANGED PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED→UNSUPPORTED. Sufficient to decide. The finding's actual allegation is 'entirely fabricated and misleading, P0, must block' — that allegation is fully refuted by the visible 'generic anonymous case' framing. PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED requires a NARROWER version of THE FINDING to hold; the finding was about fabrication, not signposting, so no narrower fabrication claim survives → UNSUPPORTED. AMBIGUITY: if 'misleading' is read loosely and the candidate's own 'could be signposted more clearly' is treated as a narrower defect, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED is arguable — hence development-only.

exactEvidenceSpans: the passage misrepresents the source's claim about diffusion timing
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: Validity unchanged (INCONCLUSIVE); the new evidenceSufficiency coordinate now RESOLVES the v2 ambiguity. Deciding whether the passage misrepresents THE SOURCE requires the source's claim, which is not provided — materially-required evidence is absent → INSUFFICIENT_TO_DECIDE → INCONCLUSIVE. (Under v2 this looked like UNSUPPORTED-vs-INCONCLUSIVE; the sufficiency rule disambiguates: missing required evidence is INCONCLUSIVE, not UNSUPPORTED.)

exactEvidenceSpans: Contribution mapping does not imply equal fault.
Naming your part does not mean the split was even; one person may hold most of the responsibility
cases.reasonForChangeOrNoChange: No change. Sufficient to decide (contract AND passage present). The finding alleges a contradiction, but the passage AGREES with the contract — the finding's own quoted evidence shows agreement, not contradiction → UNSUPPORTED.
